objective: In labstack/echo, the Decompress middleware swaps the request body for a gzip reader but leaves Request.ContentLength set to the COMPRESSED size. Downstream middleware that trusts ContentLength as the decoded body size — notably BodyLimit — then rejects or mis-sizes requests, because after streaming decompression the decoded length is unknown. Align the Decompress middleware with the net/http contract that ContentLength must be -1 (unknown) once the body is a stream whose length is not known ahead of time, so BodyLimit measures the actual decoded bytes rather than the compressed count.

explorationSubQuestions.question: After echo's Decompress middleware replaces the request body with a gzip.Reader stream at this pinned revision, what value must Request.ContentLength hold per the net/http convention, and which downstream middleware misbehaves if it is left as the compressed length?
explorationSubQuestions.groundTruth: Per net/http, ContentLength must be -1 when the body length is unknown (a decompression stream), so Decompress must set c.Request().ContentLength = -1 after swapping the body; otherwise BodyLimit compares against the compressed Content-Length and can reject or mis-size valid requests.
